newsitem.title: USA: Union pilots not optimistic on settling American dispute.
newsitem.headline: Union pilots not optimistic on settling American dispute.

text.p: Union pilots said on Friday they were not optimistic a new contract could be reached with American Airlines by the midnight deadline to avert a strike against the nation's No. 2 carrier.

"I can't say I'm optimistic at this point," said David Bates, a spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association. He made the comment to reporters amid around-the-clock talks trying to head off the work stoppage.
Bates, asked to comment on American's reaction to the pilots' last settlement offer, said, "We're disappointed that American has not accepted our proposal on the regional jet issue."

In addition to a general wage dispute, the pilots and American are in dispute over whether the union's pilots will fly new regional jets American plans to buy for its commuter line or whether those would be flown by lower paid pilots who are members of another union.

Bates, who said discussions with a federal mediator were continuing thoroughout the day, restated the pilots' pledge made earlier that if there was no agreement by midnight, "the pilots will go on strike."
He said the union plans a news conference later this afternoon. American has announced no news conference of its own.
